title: Superclasses/Traits Containing Subclass-Specific Behavior (Leaky Abstractions)
pattern: Putting specialized methods in a shared superclass or trait that are only applicable to a subset of implementations, forcing the others to write dummy or panic implementations.
why_bad: It erodes the integrity of the abstraction. Callers are forced to know the specific implementer's quirks to avoid calling invalid methods (like checking engine status on a bicycle), leading to fragile client-side logic.
detection: A trait implementation containing multiple methods that do nothing, return arbitrary dummy defaults, or panic with "not supported" errors.
counterexample: Algebraic data types (closed enums) where the absence of a behavior is structurally modeled via `Option` values.
source: Sandi Metz *POODR*, Chapter 7.2.2: "Insist on the Abstraction", p. 158, 196.
